Server provides tools organized by scope. Each higher scope includes all tools from the lower scopes. Read-only Tools – mcp.read Read-only tools for searching, fetching, and exploring your Close data. Activity Search – activity_search Search for activities. Results are returned ordered by date descending. Examples: To list activities on a lead, use the lead_ids filter. To list conversations, filter for calls and meetings. Filter for Email to get individual messages, or EmailThread to get one result per conversation. An unfiltered search returns both. Aggregate Objects – aggregate_objects Count, sum, average or otherwise aggregate CRM objects, grouped by up to two fields and optionally by time buckets. Takes the same object types and filters as list_objects. Close Product Knowledge Search – close_product_knowledge_search Search Close product documentation and knowledge base for relevant information. Use this tool when users ask about: How to use specific Close features Close API documentation and integration Workflow automation and best practices Product capabilities and limitations Setup and configuration guidance Example queries: “How do I set up automated lead assignment?” “What are Close’s API rate limits?” “How to create custom fields in Close?” “Best practices for email templates in Close” Customized Builtin Labels – customized_builtin_labels Return the customized builtin labels. Only renamed labels are returned - an empty result means the default names apply. Describe Fields – describe_fields List the fields of one object type for list_objects and aggregate_objects: built-in fields, smart fields (num_ , last_ , first_ , time_to_ , …) and the organization’s custom fields, with their value types, enum values and choices. Call it when the field you need is not in the field list of your instructions, to get the exact option strings of a choices custom field, after a validation error names an unknown field, or before concluding that nothing matches a question. Narrow with name_contains: words of the field name, of its display name, or of one of its enum values or choices. When no field has every word, the closest fields are returned and status says so. Fetch Skill – fetch_agent_skill Read a skill’s full instructions by its ID. Fetch Blackout Calendar – fetch_blackout_calendar Fetch a Blackout Date calendar and all of its date ranges by ID. Fetch Call Task – fetch_call_task Fetch a single call task by ID. Fetch Custom Object Type – fetch_custom_object_type Fetch a single custom object type by its ID. A custom object type defines the shape of a category of custom objects, including the custom fields its instances hold. Returns the type with its custom fields. Fetch Email – fetch_email Fetch a single email activity by ID. Fetch Invoice – fetch_invoice Fetch one of the organization’s billing invoices by id. Fetch Meeting – fetch_meeting Fetch a meeting activity by ID, including its user note. Use fetch_meeting_transcript for what was said in the meeting. Fetch Meeting Transcript – fetch_meeting_transcript Fetch a meeting’s Notetaker transcript(s) by meeting activity ID. Returns the meeting’s speaker breakdown, summary, and full speaker-labeled transcript text. Only covers Notetaker (meeting) transcripts; call transcripts are served by fetch_call . Fetch Membership – fetch_membership Fetch one of the organization’s members by user id. Fetch Inbox Item – fetch_notification Fetch an item in the current user’s inbox by ID, with the fields its type adds, such as an email’s triage flags or a task’s full text. Fetch Objects – fetch_objects Fetch CRM objects by their IDs, with full details: up to 30 per call. Use it when you already have the IDs, from list_objects results or from the user. To search or filter, use list_objects. IDs that don’t exist or aren’t accessible come back in not_found . Supported: leads (lead_ ), contacts (cont_ ), opportunities (oppo_ ), custom objects (custobj_ ), tasks (task_ ), activities (acti_ : emails, email threads, calls, SMS, WhatsApp, meetings, notes, completed tasks, lead and opportunity status changes, lead merges, custom activities), lead and opportunity statuses (stat_ ), pipelines with their statuses (pipe_ ), email templates (tmpl_ ), SMS templates (smstmpl_ ), Smart Views (save_ ), users (user_ ) and workflows (seq_*). Activities include user and contact names, transcripts and attachments. A lead comes with a ready-made brief in summaries : status and key fields, opportunities, open tasks, the last contact and about 30 days of recent activity. Use it directly to summarize or prepare for a lead. An email thread embeds its most recent emails in full and lists older ones in remaining_email_ids , which this tool fetches too. Fetch Primary Inbox Tab Categories – fetch_primary_inbox_view Fetch the categories the current user’s Primary inbox tab shows, as set in Customize Primary Tab. Fetch Role – fetch_role Fetch one of the organization’s roles by id, with every permission it grants. Use list_roles to resolve a role name to its id. Fetch Smart View – fetch_smart_view Fetch a smart view (saved search) of any type by ID. Return its metadata, not its search criteria. Fetch SMS – fetch_sms Fetch a single SMS activity by ID. Returns the complete SMS, including message text and attachments. Find Agent Configs – find_agent_configs List all voice agents configured for the organization. Voice agents are AI callers that place outbound calls to leads’ contacts on the user’s behalf. Returns each voice agent’s ID, name and whether it is active. Use this to find the right voice agent ID when scheduling a call or assigning a call step in a workflow. Users may refer to voice agents as “voice agents”, “Chloe”, or by their configured name. When more than one agent exists, pick the most appropriate one based on the name. Find Skills – find_agent_skills List skills, saved instructions for Close’s in-app AI agents, that are available to the user. Most recently used first. Read a skill’s instructions with fetch_agent_skill . Find Blackout Calendars – find_blackout_calendars List Blackout Date calendars, optionally by name or auto-select setting. Fetch a calendar with fetch_blackout_calendar to read its dates before proposing changes. Find Call Outcomes – find_call_outcomes List currently configured call outcomes and their descriptions. Omit agent_config_id for all organization call outcomes. Supply it for a voice agent’s available outcomes; agents without a conversation type use all organization call outcomes. Requires ViewVoiceAgents when supplied. Find Call Tasks – find_call_tasks Find call tasks based on various filters. You can filter by lead, contact, assignee (a user or a voice agent), completion state, and scheduled/created/updated dates. List Contact Custom Fields – find_contact_custom_fields List all contact custom fields defined for the organization. Includes both contact-specific fields and shared fields associated with contacts. Returns each field’s ID, name, description, type, allowed choices (for choice fields), whether multiple values are accepted, and whether it is a shared field. Useful for deciding which custom field to read or write when working with contacts. Find Contacts – find_contacts Find contacts with simple filters, ordered by last updated descending. Omit filters to list recent contacts. Filters combine with AND; IDs within each list combine with OR. Name matches the beginning of words in the contact name only. Email matches an exact address ignoring case. Both email and phone match secondary entries, not just the primary one. Phone matches a complete number after normalization, not a suffix. E.164 is not required: +1 (415) 555-0142 and (415) 555-0142 are accepted. Without a country code, numbers use the requesting user’s country. Include the area code where required, such as for U.S. numbers. Ask for missing dialing information instead of guessing it. Each preview row has an id, type, and fields in this fixed order: name, primary_email, primary_phone, title, lead_id. The lead reference has a ref: prefix. Use fetch_objects for full records and secondary entries. query_id identifies the shared entry for these results. For the next page, pass only next_cursor as cursor to find_contacts. Use list_objects for other filters, columns, or sorting, and aggregate_objects for counts and totals. Find Custom Activity Types – find_custom_activities List all active (non-archived) Custom Activity Types in the organization, along with the custom fields defined on each type. Call this before creating a workflow with a “custom-activity-event” trigger so you can look up the correct Custom Activity Type ID. Find Custom Activity Instances – find_custom_activity_instances Find a lead’s custom activity instances based on various filters. A custom activity instance is an activity of a custom activity type, holding the custom field values defined by that type. Always scoped to a single lead; optionally filter by attributed user, one or more custom activity types, or activity date. Results are sorted by most recent activity first and are cursor-paginated. Find Custom Object Instances – find_custom_object_instances Find a lead’s custom object instances. A custom object instance is a record of a custom object type, attached to a lead and holding the custom field values defined by that type. Always scoped to a single lead; optionally filter to a single custom object type. Results are ordered by creation date (oldest first) and are cursor-paginated. Find Custom Object Types – find_custom_object_types List all custom object types in the organization, along with the custom fields defined on each type. Find Email Templates – find_email_templates List or find email templates Find Web Forms – find_forms List all web forms in the organization. Call this before creating a workflow with a “form-submission-event” trigger so you can look up the correct Form ID. Find Groups – find_groups List all groups in the organization. Find Invoices – find_invoices Find the organization’s billing invoices, newest first. Invoices without a date sort first. List Lead Custom Fields – find_lead_custom_fields List all lead custom fields defined for the organization. Returns each field’s ID, name, description, type, allowed choices (for choice fields), whether multiple values are accepted, and whether it is a shared field. Useful for deciding which custom field to read or write when working with leads. Find Lead Statuses – find_lead_statuses List or find lead statuses for the organization Find Leads – find_leads Find leads with simple filters, ordered by last updated descending. Omit filters to list recent leads. Filters combine with AND; IDs within each list combine with OR. Name matches only the lead name, not contact names. Name and full_text match the beginning of words. Each preview row has an id, type, and fields in this fixed order: name, status_id. Status references have a status: prefix, and refs maps each one to its status name. Use fetch_objects for full records. query_id identifies the shared entry for these results. For the next page, pass only next_cursor as cursor to find_leads. Use list_objects for other filters, columns, or sorting, and aggregate_objects for counts and totals. Find Meeting Outcomes – find_meeting_outcomes List all outcomes applicable to meetings available in the organization. Find Memberships – find_memberships List the organization’s members with each member’s role name, whether the role is built-in or custom, active/inactive status, and join date. Richer than org_users — prefer this unless you only need a name or email. Most recent members first. Find Notes – find_notes Find notes based on various filters. Find Inbox Items – find_notifications Find items in the current user’s inbox, such as incoming emails and SMS, missed calls, voicemails, tasks, and drafts waiting for review. By default returns the items in the inbox today. Find Opportunities – find_opportunities Find opportunities by status (active/won/lost), owner, lead, or close-date range, optionally only those needing attention, sorted by soonest close, largest value, or highest confidence. Returns each opportunity with resolved lead, contact, owner, and status names; cursor-paginated. List Opportunity Custom Fields – find_opportunity_custom_fields List all opportunity custom fields defined for the organization. Includes both opportunity-specific fields and shared fields associated with opportunities. Returns each field’s ID, name, description, type, allowed choices (for choice fields), whether multiple values are accepted, and whether it is a shared field. Useful for deciding which custom field to read or write when working with opportunities. Find Phone Numbers – find_phone_numbers List phone numbers visible to the current user for administration. Users with Manage Team Phone Numbers permission see every number in the organization. Other users see numbers they belong to, directly or through an assigned Group. Find Pipelines – find_pipelines_and_opportunity_statuses List all opportunity pipelines and their opportunity statuses in the organization. Find Rentable Phone Numbers – find_rentable_phone_numbers List phone numbers available to rent in the requested country. Find Scheduling Links – find_scheduling_links List available scheduling links for the user and org. User-owned personal links come with a URL. Shared links come with a special template tag. Each can be inserted into generated templates. Find Smart Views – find_smart_views List smart views (saved searches) of every type that the user can see. Without pinned_only , the most recently updated smart views come first. Find SMS Templates – find_sms_templates List or find SMS templates Find Tasks – find_tasks Find tasks based on various filters. You can filter by lead, assignee, completion state, and due/created/ updated dates. Find Voice Agents – find_voice_agents List all voice agents configured for the organization. Voice agents are AI callers that place outbound calls to leads’ contacts on the user’s behalf. Returns each voice agent’s ID, name and whether it is active. Use this to find the right voice agent ID when scheduling a call or assigning a call step in a workflow. Users may refer to voice agents as “voice agents”, “Chloe”, or by their configured name. When more than one agent exists, pick the most appropriate one based on the name. Find Workflows – find_workflows List or find workflows Get AI Credit Usage – get_ai_credit_usage AI credit usage for the billing account, broken down by feature. Reports total credits used and a per-feature breakdown. Credits are the billing unit for AI features. Usage covers the whole billing account, not a single organization. Omit start / end for the current billing period; the result’s start / end report the window actually measured. Explicit ranges must be timezone-aware and span at most 366 days. Older ranges may return empty or partial data — zero usage for an old range does not mean no activity. On a rate-limited error, retry after retry_after seconds. Get Billing Summary – get_billing_summary Billing summary for the organization’s billing account. Reports the subscription plan, billing status with the trial end date, seat counts, and AI usage availability, tier, and credit allowance for the current billing cycle. Whether the account is on trial is status , not anything under ai_usage . Use get_ai_credit_usage for the credits actually used. Get Voice Agent Overview Report – get_voice_agent_overview_report Cross-agent rollup for the Voice Agents list page. Returns one row per active agent — agents with completed calls in date_range or queued upcoming calls. Cumulative funnel counts ( answered , engaged , objective_met ) plus total_calls . upcoming_calls is the agent’s queued (not yet completed) calls and is not bound by date_range — open tasks are open regardless of when scheduled (so an agent with only upcoming calls still appears). Use this to compare agents; for one agent’s outcomes, sentiment, or time saved use get_voice_agent_performance_report . For an inventory of all configured voice agents regardless of activity, use find_agent_configs . The Voice Agents list (Agents tab) shows all-time stats, so leave date_range at its default ( all_time ) unless the user asks for a specific window. (The Upcoming and Recent tabs are call lists, not this rollup — search Calls for those.) Rows are sorted server-side per the sort field (default most_calls ); pass a different mode rather than re-sorting in your reply. Set reverse=True to invert (e.g. sort=most_calls, reverse=True for least active first) — necessary to surface the bottom of the ordering, since rows are capped before they reach you. truncated and total_agent_count flag in-scope active agents; dormant_agent_count reports in-scope agents with neither completed calls in the date range nor queued upcoming calls (not included in rows ). Get Voice Agent Performance Report – get_voice_agent_performance_report Performance metrics for one voice agent. Returns the numbers shown on the Performance tab of a Voice Agent detail page. Passing multiple agent_config_ids pools metrics into a single aggregate (not a per-agent breakdown — for that, use get_voice_agent_overview_report ). For per-call drill-down, search Calls filtered by agent_config_id . When the user is on a Voice Agent page, pull date_range from page_context.date_range so the numbers match the UI. Accepts a relative range such as last_week or an absolute period with type="absolute" , start , and end . For a stored recap, use its inclusive timeframe_start and exclusive timeframe_end . Outcome coverage uses answered_by_disposition_count ; answered_count is the funnel’s Human Reached count. Percentages: *_pct is over total_calls ; engaged_over_answered_pct and objective_met_over_answered_pct are over answered (tier-to-tier conversion). For any other denominator, compute from *_count . issue_signals contains active improvement suggestions for one agent, using the Performance tab’s medium confidence / 5 occurrence threshold. The date range selects agent snapshots, not individual occurrences: issue counts and examples may extend outside the report period. This field is null for multiple agents or restricted lead visibility. funnel_previous_period_deltas is null when the date range has no defined previous period (e.g. all_time ). Get Voice Agents – get_voice_agents Return detailed configuration for one or more voice agents. Includes each agent’s objective, user instructions, and which skills are enabled. Use this as the follow-up to find_voice_agents once one or more agent IDs have been selected. Lead Search – lead_search Perform a simple lead search and return the initial set of results. Use this to retrieve all leads, most recent leads, search leads by keyword, or filter by lead status and smart view. For more complex searches use the search tool instead. Leads will be returned by last updated first. List Membership Requests – list_membership_requests List pending requests to join the current organization. Each entry includes the requesting user’s name and email, the request id, and when the request was created. List Objects – list_objects Search and list CRM objects (leads, contacts, opportunities, tasks, activities and more) with a structured query of filters, columns and sort. Each preview row has the object’s id and type, and fields : one value per requested column, in the order of columns . A column that doesn’t apply to the row’s type is an empty string. Referenced users, statuses and objects are prefixed IDs ( user: , status: , ref: ). refs maps each of those IDs to its name, so you don’t need to fetch them just to name them; fetch_objects returns the full objects. For the next page, pass only the result’s next_cursor as cursor ; the page comes back in the same columns. To answer “how many” or “how much”, use aggregate_objects instead of paging through the list. Nested object types have no IDs and can’t be listed; they only filter their parents, like leads by address. List Roles – list_roles List the roles that can be assigned in the organization. Covers Close’s built-in roles plus any custom roles the org defines. Use this to resolve a role name to its id, or to see which roles grant organization management access. Org Info – org_info Return general information about the organization and the user. Org Users – org_users Return active users (memberships) which are part of the current org. Paginate Search Results – paginate_search Paginate a search to retrieve more results. Provide exactly one of: search_id : a share_* id from a previous search or shared entry, or smart_view_id : a save_* Smart View (saved search) id the user is viewing. Propose Voice Agent Update – propose_voice_agent_update Propose a voice agent configuration update from natural-language feedback. This tool does not apply changes to the voice agent. It returns a short behavioral summary and proposal ID when the requested edit is clear. If the feedback is ambiguous, it returns clarification questions instead of making a proposal. Use apply_voice_agent_update with the proposal ID only after the user approves the proposal. Render Email Template – render_email_template Render an email template for a lead, including any template variables. Body HTML already contains the user’s email signature, denoted with a <span data-system-generated="signature"> tag. Leave this tag intact or the signature could get duplicated later. Render SMS Template – render_sms_template Render an SMS template for a lead, including any template variables. Search Objects – search Perform a natural language search for leads or contacts. If a more specific search tool (like lead_search or activity_search) satisfies the request, use that tool instead. You can reference related objects like activities (such as calls, emails, meetings, notes, custom activities, etc.), opportunities, tasks as long as they are part of a lead query. Example queries: leads not contacted in the past week leads assigned to me with uncompleted tasks leads with an active opportunity over $500 contacts with CTO title Each returned result will contain a title label, preview text, object ID, and URL. The initial set of results, total count of all results, and a URL to open the results in Close is returned. To retrieve more results, use the returned cursor and call the paginate_search tool using the cursor and search ID returned in this response. Show Contact – show_contact Show a contact (person) to the user as a card. Call this only to present a contact to the user, usually once at the end of your answer. To read a contact’s data, use fetch_objects. Show Lead – show_lead Show a lead (company) to the user as a card. Call this only to present a lead to the user, usually once at the end of your answer. To read a lead’s data, use fetch_objects. Show Opportunities – show_opportunities Show opportunities (deals) to the user as a list. Call this only to present opportunities to the user, usually once at the end of your answer. To find opportunities, use find_opportunities. To read an opportunity’s data, use fetch_objects. Show Tasks – show_tasks Show tasks to the user as a list. Call this only to present tasks to the user, usually once at the end of your answer. To find tasks, use find_tasks. To read a task’s data, use fetch_objects. Submit Feedback – submit_feedback Send feedback to Close about this MCP integration. Report errors, confusing tool results, clunky interfaces or missing capabilities you encounter. Briefly explain the goal, what got in the way, and any workaround you used. Preserve the user’s wording if they provide a specific message to send. Do not include secrets, customer records, or the full conversation. This does not open a support ticket, it is logged for eventual consideration. Write (Safe) Tools – mcp.write_safe Includes all mcp.read scoped tools, plus these tools for creating and updating data: Create Address – create_address Add a new address to an existing lead (company). Create Skill – create_agent_skill Create a private skill for the user: instructions they can reuse with Close AI agents by typing / and picking it, which Close AI agents also follow on their own when the skill fits the request. Only create a skill when the user asks for one. Write instructions that stand on their own, without this conversation: the task, the steps and the expected output. The skill’s description is generated from them afterwards. Create Blackout Calendar – create_blackout_calendar Create a Blackout Date calendar using the same rules as Close Settings. Show the proposed dates to the user before saving. Annual recurrence repeats on the same month and day, so holidays that move each year need explicit dates for each year instead of repeats_annually. Create Comment – create_comment Add a comment to a commentable object (note, call, opportunity, task, custom object, etc.). If the object already has a comment thread, the new comment is appended to it. Otherwise a new thread is started for the object. Use this tool for both starting a conversation and replying to an existing one — the object_id alone determines which. Comments support @-mentions of users and groups. The body is HTML. Create Contact – create_contact Create a new contact for a lead. A contact represents a person associated with a lead (company). Create Custom Activity Instance – create_custom_activity_instance Create a new custom activity instance on a lead. A custom activity instance is an activity of a custom activity type, holding the custom field values defined by that type. Use the find_custom_activities tool to look up the available custom activity types. If in an interactive session, ask the user for the relevant field values (including custom fields) before creating, even if they are not required. Create Custom Object Instance – create_custom_object_instance Create a new custom object instance on a lead. A custom object instance is a record of a custom object type, attached to a lead and holding the custom field values defined by that type. Use the find_custom_object_types tool to look up the available custom object types. If in an interactive session, ask the user for the relevant field values (including custom fields) before creating, even if they are not required. Create Draft Email – create_draft_email Create a draft email on a lead. The email is saved as an unsent draft for the user to review, edit, and send from Close; it is never sent automatically. Provide the body as Close rich text (HTML) via body_html; the sender’s saved email signature is appended automatically. To create a reply in an existing thread, provide the ID of the email being replied to via in_reply_to_id. Create Draft SMS – create_draft_sms Create a draft SMS on a lead. The SMS is saved as an unsent draft for the user to review, edit, and send from Close. It is never sent or scheduled automatically. Create Email Template – create_email_template Create a new email template. Handling of attachments and unsubscribe links via this tool is currently unsupported. Email template body should be HTML formatted. Use template tags as placeholders, for example: {{ organization.name }} to refer to the sender’s organization name. {{ user.first_name }} {{ user.last_name }} {{ user.email }} {{ user.phone }} to refer to the user sending the email. {{ lead.display_name }} to refer to the lead name (recipient’s name/company). {{ contact.first_name }} {{ contact.last_name }} to refer to the recipient. Create Lead – create_lead Create a new lead (company). After creating a lead, you should usually add an address or contact (including phone or email) to the lead. Create Lead Status – create_lead_status Create a new lead status. Create Note – create_note Create a new note on a lead. A note is a text-based activity attached to a lead. At least one of note (plaintext) or note_html (rich text) must be provided. Create Opportunity – create_opportunity Create a new opportunity. Requires a lead ID and status ID. Other fields are optional. The value should be specified in cents (e.g., $100.00 = 10000). Create Opportunity Stage – create_opportunity_status_tool Create a new opportunity status. Create Pipeline – create_pipeline Create a new opportunity pipeline. Use the create_opportunity_status tool to add statuses to the pipeline. Create Smart View – create_smart_view Save a search as a smart view (saved search). Pass the ID of a search result that lists one object type: leads, contacts, opportunities, or one kind of activity. The smart view gets that search’s filters, sort, and columns, so it lists exactly what was previewed. Confirm the name and criteria with the user before creating the view. Create SMS Template – create_sms_template Create a new SMS template. Handling of attachments via this tool is currently unsupported. Use template tags as placeholders, for example: {{ organization.name }} to refer to the sender’s organization name. {{ user.first_name }} {{ user.last_name }} {{ user.email }} {{ user.phone }} to refer to the user sending the message. {{ lead.display_name }} to refer to the lead name (recipient’s name/company). {{ contact.first_name }} {{ contact.last_name }} to refer to the recipient. Create Task – create_task Create a new task for a lead. A task represents a to-do item that can be assigned to a user and optionally associated with a contact. Create Workflow – create_workflow Create a new workflow (a.k.a. sequence) with Draft status. Log Call – log_call Log a call that took place outside of Close. This records the call on the lead. It does not place a call. Pin Smart View – pin_smart_view Pin a smart view to the top of the user’s sidebar. A smart view that is already pinned moves to the top. Rent Phone Number – rent_phone_number Rent an exact internal phone number and assign it to the current user. Always use find_rentable_phone_numbers first and show the user the available numbers, their carrier types, and their monthly prices before calling this tool. Only rent a number after the user selects it. Renting creates a billable phone number for the organization. Unpin Smart View – unpin_smart_view Remove a smart view from the user’s sidebar. The smart view itself is not deleted. Write (Destructive) Tools – mcp.write_destructive Includes all mcp.read and mcp.write_safe scoped tools, plus these tools for updating and deleting data: Apply Voice Agent Update – apply_voice_agent_update Apply a previously proposed voice agent update. This tool persists the server-stored proposal identified by proposal_id. It does not rerun the feedback processor, and it fails if the proposal has expired or the voice agent changed after the proposal was created. Bulk Update Tasks – bulk_update_tasks Reassign or reprioritize several of the current user’s tasks at once. To move due dates, use snooze_notifications. To complete tasks, use mark_notifications_done. ONLY call this if the user asked to change these tasks. Cancel Email Send – cancel_email_send Cancel a queued or scheduled email send and keep the email as an unsent draft. Only emails in outbox or scheduled status can be canceled. The email is not deleted. Cancellation fails if the email is already being sent. Cancel SMS Send – cancel_sms_send Cancel a queued or scheduled SMS send and keep the SMS as an unsent draft. Only SMS messages in outbox or scheduled status can be canceled. The SMS is not deleted. Cancellation fails if the SMS is already being sent. Create Call Task – create_call_task Schedule a call task on a lead, assigned to either a user or a voice agent (Chloe). A call task represents a scheduled outbound call that will be made to the specified contact at the given time. The task can be assigned to a specific user or dispatched to a voice agent. Delete Address – delete_address Delete an address from an existing lead (company) if there is an exact match. Delete Call Task – delete_call_task Delete a call task. Does not affect sibling tasks. Delete Comment – delete_comment Delete a comment. The comment’s content is removed. If it was the only remaining comment in its thread, the whole thread is deleted. This action cannot be undone. ONLY call this if the user specifically instructed you to delete the comment. Delete Contact – delete_contact Permanently delete an existing contact. This will remove the contact from its lead including its email addresses, phone numbers, and URLs will be removed. Activities on the lead are not affected. This action cannot be undone. ONLY call this if the user specifically instructed you to delete the contact. Delete Custom Activity Instance – delete_custom_activity_instance Permanently delete an existing custom activity instance. This action cannot be undone. ONLY call this if the user specifically instructed you to delete the custom activity instance. Delete Custom Object Instance – delete_custom_object_instance Permanently delete an existing custom object instance. A custom object instance is a record of a custom object type, attached to a lead and holding the custom field values defined by that type. This action cannot be undone.
